title: UPDATE: AI Bots Originally Used Against Iran Now Support Benjamin Netanyahu on X
summary:
The use of generative AI and deepfake videos became a central feature of the Oct 27 Knesset elections as both sides of Israel's political divide flooded the social media platform X to reach voters. Reports from Israeli media indicate that bot networks now used to disseminate pro-Benjamin Netanyahu messages were originally created to target the government of Iran, signaling a shift in how the prime minister's campaign is deploying digital influence tools.

The reports on the election's online activity follow a series of crackdowns by the Shin Bet and Israeli national police, who removed accounts linked to foreign influence campaigns in the run-up to the vote. Netanyahu has repeatedly warned that Mossad and military intelligence detected Iranian plots to undermine the election's integrity through cyberattacks and security incidents, while some security sources warned Tehran might attempt to influence the outcome by driving up global oil prices.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Numerous social media profiles used as part of a "foreign influence campaign" were removed from the internet ahead of the election, the Shin Bet security agency says.
selectedTweets.text:
Numerous social media profiles used as part of a "foreign influence campaign" were removed from the internet ahead of the election, the Shin Bet security agency says.

The Shin Bet says it worked with the Cyber Department in the State Attorney's Office and the Central Elections Committee to identify the profiles.

"As part of the joint effort to safeguard the integrity of the elections and thwart attempts at improper foreign influence, these accounts were removed from the internet," the security agency says.
